reviews.text: 找到个画风很可爱的游戏，有点像rpg的养成但是是肉鸽，挺好玩的。画风很讨喜武器也还蛮多的，就是不知道后面能不能出一个可以保存装备的模式，每次玩到后面都有点舍不得自己的队员和装备。好评！

[h1]《魔法书自走棋：契约》姗姗来迟的精品自走棋[/h1] 其实游戏本身不错，唯一可惜的就是进场太迟了，真的太迟了，自走棋的热度已经下降到了很多人体验过类似的游戏了。游戏要是能早在春节前出来，那想必应该也会获得更多的喜爱。（毕竟游戏性质算是半休闲，没有办法挂机游玩，所以在现在这个又是上班又是上学的日子里，玩家能空出来的游玩时间不会很多） 略过那些话题，也直接略过简单的故事背景，我们直接来说游戏。游戏的内容其实还是比较多的。相对于以往精简的自走棋，这款游戏在建模上就已经做的比较不错的。在武器的种类上，更是有六十左右。哪怕是同样的一种武器，例如盾牌，也有多个不同的盾牌，带来的属性侧重以及带来的技能都不一样。在给我们选择的构筑上，也是变得丰富多样。加上不同的角色，给的基础属性也会有差异，哪怕是同样一个角色，给与的被动也都不一样，所以选择也要慎重。 游戏的简介说是RPG+自走棋，游戏中的RPG元素就在于装备的合成和重铸（相同品质的三件同个装备可以合成下一级装备，相同品质的不同装备概率重铸为下一品级的随机装备），还有就是经验，每次战斗亦或是事件中我们都可以获得经验，经验可以提升角色等级，等级提升会获得属性增益以及解锁新的被动。（缺点就是我好像找不到去哪里看经验有多少以及升级经验花费多少） 游戏还给各种BOSS设计了不同的形象和技能，祝福和我们角色的技能也足够绚烂多彩，整体来说还是个不错的游戏。 [code] [h1]欢迎关注 [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/luanqibajiao]乱七芭蕉[/url][/b] 鉴赏家[/h1] 欢迎各路 [strike]肥宅、哲学家、LSP、绅士[/strike] 大神和小白加入我们：[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/luanqibajiao][b]乱七芭蕉[/b][/url] 一起分享乱七芭蕉的 [strike]福利资源[/strike] 游戏经验：[b]Q群774704264[/b] [/code]

推荐入手。完成度挺高，总体上还是很有趣的，但还有很多可以优化的地方。 一个是战斗结算界面，角色表现里可以把护盾值也加上，输出/承伤可以按物理/魔法分别展示，最好能在子选项中查看伤害来源 另一个是词条介绍太过简略，比如BOSS算不算精英怪，灼烧伤害跟层数有没关系会不会叠加，某些职业非主属性的属性会不会影响伤害，光是看现有的词条解释根本无法理解。 还有一个是非武器装备（头和肩）的套装属性居然有完全的上位替代，我感觉是套装词条重复度太高，建议把区分做的明显一点。 最后一个要提一下随机事件，不点进去压根不知道这个选项是干嘛的，建议增加鼠标悬停时弹个简介，大致说一下可能获得的东西（武器/装备/经验等），这样对新手友好点。 值得鼓励支持。

[h1] 构建羁绊组建队伍，熔炼装备不断提升[/h1] 因发行商问题而遭下架的《魔法书自走棋》如今重新上线，游戏采用了装备养成为核心的小队构建+简单轻松的全自动战斗形式。通过商店刷新购买、铁匠铺重铸合成，构建8人小队并搭配武器、头盔、披肩、饰品，每名小队成员的职业都由所装备的武器类型决定，头盔与披肩则可以组成套装，并共同提供了六大职业的羁绊点数，相当于自走棋的凑羁绊元素由角色转移到了装备上。（战士、守护、游侠、盗贼、法师、祭司） [h1] 无需操作，重在配队，并尝试新的策略[/h1] 由于自走棋无需操作的战斗形式，玩家要做的就是挑选适合的装备、用之提升战力、配置人员和装备来壮大小队，并挑选能够打过、或者获益最高的敌人来挑战。随着战斗胜利次数上升、面对同样变强的敌人，在此流程下不断重复、不断培养队伍。不同的装备也诞生了多样的组合，使得玩家可以尝试各种战术，从经典的战法牧混搭，或者清一色的肉坦奶，不断探索自己最喜欢的一种策略搭配。 [h1] 轻松休闲消磨时间，变化不足易感乏味[/h1] 总之，就是和“矮人军团自走棋”很相似的一套玩法，卡通画风更舒适精致，增添了人物升级与随机事件，在羁绊系统上也有所调整。整体物美价廉、简单轻松，依靠丰富的装备带来多样的build，看着自己所搭配出的队伍组合取得一场又一场的胜利也充满了乐趣，能够消磨不少时间；缺点则在于，玩法上的变化稍显不足，后期很容易陷入一种自己只是在单纯刷商品、刷人物、凑装备的枯燥观感，可能算是这类游戏的通病；对于之前有玩过相似游戏玩家而言，这种乏味的到来也会更加迅速。 [h1]总结[/h1] 整体仍是一款不错的休闲游戏，其中游戏乐趣的重要一部分便在于思考配队策略、并在一局当中逐步实现，推荐喜欢自走棋类型的玩家入手尝试！ [quote]加入[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/GHYX]干货游戏[/url]&关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35106417/]咱的鉴赏家[/url]，不定期为大家带来游戏体验分享，也期待您来一起分享自己的游戏体验干货~[/quote]

This game is a little gem. An addictive one as well. You build your team from several types of heroes and kill monsters and bosses. You must have synergies, like using burn/fire or ice/frozen. I still not have all the data because not all the equipment has unlocked for me. It unlocks in the game, when you try to craft it and on the meta progression after each run, successful or not. It has some peaks of difficulty, mainly in the beginning, if you can't find the heroes or the equipment you want. For example, I lost a run because I couldn't find in the shop a bow or a gun for my archer and he had to use the novice one. I'd forgotten to put it in the settings of the run and had bad luck with this. The long and short of it: for the great price, I recommend the game for a mostly relaxing experience. Pros: - nice graphics, cartoonish and funny - good synergies and challenge (mostly at the beginning) - good feeling of progression either in the run or at meta level - addictive in a good way - no bugs, runs smoothly - very good price for what you get, similar games are a lot more expensive Cons: - some item descriptions are not translated in English (yet, I hope).

Edit --- Played a bit more after the patch. More content. Still unreadable. Again: lots of good ideas/ mechanics, but not made easy to be played and built upon. Devs are not focus on the things that would improve their game imo. (Still inconsistent gameplay words, unclear definitions and mechanics, missing information in codex, etc.) Previous review --- It s a "fun" game. In a mindless way. Really entertaining to discover but really annoying to dig in. The concept is really good and the art fresh, but the execution is poor. I think it s a good base but other devs will be able to greatly improve this formula. Pass on it and wait for an upgraded version, probably by someone else. In this state, it is not worth imo. The mechanics are quite simple: you get a team of 8 to go dungeon-crawling, you shop and you auto-battle. Lots of rpg elements, lots of tier and content. The game feels cosy. But then it gets messy when you realise the basics are not there: - A lot of information is visually missing: no hp bar for mobs, no shield bar (at all), no icon for most effects (and the icons that exists are not explained), no icon for your stacking buffs/ debuffs ... you dont know if what you are doing is working or not. There are only healing/damage numbers popping up, a lot of them, with different colors. Pretty. Messy. - The translation is not consistent on the basic terms. For example, "Power" and "Strengh" are the same, but there are 2 words for it. "Poison" and "Corrosion" are the same (i think). A lot of different aspect of the game are referred in 2 or 3 different ways. It gets confusing rapidly. - The written explanations of the mechanics and complex effects are lacking (missing duration of effects, if they stack or are consecutive, the type of damage, if it triggers other effects or not, etc.). I still dont know if attacking with a weapon that attacks 2 times the same mob is considered as one auto-attack or two (quite important for certain items), and I cant check in-game because there are no visuals cues... - The index is a mess. For the armor you discovered, you have the flavor text, but no stats. For the weapons you have the description of their skills, but not their stats... It s like playing TFT without any HUD, no wiki and google translate. It s fun at first because not much is needed. A few clicks and stuff happens on the screen. But trying to go to the higher difficulty gets irritating as you dont know if your combos work: most of my playtime is me trying to understand the game instead of playing it. Meh.

In early game: - The tutorial is bad, it only says things that I already can see because I have eyes, like "hey this is the black smith, this is the shop,...", not showing any example of what I can do with it. - There's a milestone where I always get there and can't get pass unless I have died and bought enough upgrades. In late game, when I reached level 100 and more in Endless Mode, the game starting to get bored: - Weapons and armors are limitted to tier Red+1, can't upgrade them further. Accessories and Blessings can't be upgraded. - Weapons have pretty good varietty but you can only pick some at the start of each run. If you wanna experience other weapons, you have to restart, can't change in middle of a run. All of those means there's another milestone at late game keep me from enjoying the game more.

既然官方还挺听劝，再说几点建议： 一是后期数值很抽象，打25000块钱+的能碾压，打2000块钱+的反而暴毙，有一把挑战340层精英怪轻松过，341层普通怪反而死活过不去，怪的盾都打不掉就嗝屁了...就算是挑战模式有点难可以理解，但是得让我死个明白吧。 二是装备成长，现在看着装备可以无限升级，好像能追上或超过怪物属性数值是的，其实后期费半天劲装备+7升+8数值也就长了10来点，装备整体属性和套装属性基本没提升，对比怪物属性成长曲线太小。 三是魔法书能量，后期升一级本来就不容易，魔法书能量还是两级长5点，所谓的羁绊自由搭配几乎不可能实现，翻来覆去常用的也就那几样。 四是能不能继续优化一下，平时都正常，队友阵亡屏幕就卡一下，电脑配置肯定没问题，队友死本来没什么影响，其他人足够把对面灭了，结果这一卡剩下的人也放不出技能了，反应过来团灭了... 最后吐槽一下每90层换装备的设定，我想官方设定的初衷应该是好的，但能不能加个选择开关，谁没事就换？不换也得点，白白给怪加一大层buff...

Magicbook AutoBattler: Contract is a single-player-focused auto battler that blends classic auto-chess foundations with RPG-style progression and roguelike unpredictability. Developed and published by JXGS, the game is built around the idea of mastering preparation rather than execution, asking players to assemble, equip, and synergize a team of adventurers before watching battles resolve automatically. What distinguishes it from many genre peers is its clear commitment to a solo experience, framing each run as a self-contained contract within a magical grimoire rather than a competitive multiplayer contest. The core loop revolves around recruiting adventurers and shaping them into a cohesive squad through careful positioning and equipment choices. Players can field a sizable team, and each unit fulfills a recognizable fantasy role—warriors, priests, thieves, rangers, and more—yet their effectiveness depends heavily on how they interact with gear sets, weapons, and passive bonuses. The preparation phase becomes the true battleground, as even small changes in formation or loadout can dramatically alter outcomes. This emphasis on planning gives the game a thoughtful pace that rewards foresight and adaptability rather than reflexes. Customization is one of the game’s strongest features. A large pool of weapons and suit sets allows for deep experimentation, encouraging players to chase synergies rather than raw stats. Equipment can fundamentally change how a character behaves in combat, turning familiar roles into something more specialized or unexpected. Over the course of a run, players are also presented with blessings, bonds, and random events that further shape their strategy, often forcing difficult choices between immediate power and long-term potential. This layered system ensures that no two playthroughs feel exactly the same. Combat itself unfolds automatically, but it remains engaging because of the clarity with which results reflect player decisions. When a strategy succeeds, it feels earned, and when it fails, the cause is usually traceable back to preparation choices rather than hidden randomness. Boss encounters in particular serve as meaningful tests of team composition and synergy, often requiring players to rethink their approach instead of simply upgrading numbers. Difficulty spikes can be sharp, but they tend to reinforce learning rather than punish blindly, pushing players to explore alternative builds or tactics. The game also incorporates a light narrative framework through its concept of contracts and the magical book that binds each run together. While storytelling is not the main focus, this framing gives context to progression and helps unify the experience. Events between battles add flavor and decision-making opportunities, occasionally presenting moral or strategic dilemmas that affect future encounters. These moments break up the rhythm of combat preparation and add a sense of journey to what could otherwise feel purely mechanical. Visually, Magicbook AutoBattler: Contract is more polished than many indie titles in the genre. Character animations and spell effects bring clarity to battles, making it easier to understand how abilities interact and why certain outcomes occur. The art style leans into colorful fantasy without overwhelming the screen, which is important in a game where readability directly impacts strategic understanding. The interface presents a lot of information, but it is generally organized in a way that allows players to make informed decisions without excessive friction. Despite its strengths, the game does have areas that may challenge some players. The depth of its systems can be intimidating at first, especially for those new to auto battlers or roguelike structure. Tooltips and explanations are present, but the learning curve still requires patience as mechanics reveal their full importance over time. Balance can also feel uneven in certain runs, with luck playing a noticeable role in which options become available, though this randomness is largely in line with the genre’s expectations. Overall, Magicbook AutoBattler: Contract delivers a thoughtful and replayable single-player auto battler that prioritizes strategic depth and experimentation. Its rich customization systems, strong emphasis on preparation, and roguelike structure make it especially appealing to players who enjoy refining builds and adapting to evolving challenges. While it demands time and attention to fully appreciate its mechanics, it rewards that investment with a satisfying sense of mastery and variety, standing as a solid option for fans of solo-focused strategy games. Rating: 7/10
